assignments.title: When programmable processing-in-memory wins after the full data path is charged
assignments.finite_question: On the real UPMEM DPU platform, which workload and data-placement conditions yield a full-system benefit over CPU or GPU execution once host orchestration, data movement, setup, and result collection are included? Compare the experimental PrIM characterization with the later offload-aware evaluation, and use the architecture-level PIMulator study only to explain mechanisms that those measurements cannot isolate.
assignments.breadth_and_counterevidence: Compare measurement boundaries and workload classes rather than aggregating speedups across papers. For each representative win and loss, record operation, data volume/reuse, partitioning and placement, host and accelerator baselines, device/software generation, and whether the reported time includes input staging, transfer, configuration/launch, kernel, and output collection. Separate measured UPMEM hardware results from PIMulator simulation. Identify evidence for bandwidth, DPU compute, local-memory capacity, memory interleaving, host orchestration, and transfer costs only when the cited source measures or models that mechanism. Include at least one case in which an apparently PIM-friendly kernel result changes under full-system accounting and one case that remains favorable under the paper's complete boundary. End with a short evaluation checklist for GPU/ASIC offload studies; label that checklist as transferable inference, not a UPMEM result or a Strata recommendation.
assignments.novelty_guard: Scope is real UPMEM programmable DPU PIM and its end-to-end accounting. It is not a survey of all PIM/CIM technologies and does not generalize UPMEM findings to HBM-PIM, analog in-memory compute, GPUs, Intel Arc, or Strata. R779 is irregular gather/cache-page behavior, R786 is destination contention and reduction strategy, and R873 is ASIC fully-connected dataflow; use those as metadata boundaries only and do not repeat them. Exclude XeStrata, code adaptation, local source, implementation advice, local tests/builds/GPU/profiler/process inspection, and claims about the current system.
assignments.report_budget: 1,400-1,700 substantive words, no more than 6 primary URLs, one compact table separating workload, timing boundary, and winning platform; at least one measured counterexample; source-specific hardware and evidence limits.
prerequisites: Public access to the three original UPMEM/PIM sources listed below.
No local GPU, code, build, test, profiler, process, or product result is required.
assignments.prerequisite_evidence: The public arXiv record for the 2022 PrIM hardware characterization, the author-hosted DIMES 2023 full-system study, and the 2024 HPCA PIMulator study are accessible primary sources. They provide complementary measured-hardware, offload-inclusive, and simulation evidence. Index text contains no earlier PIM or near-data collection; adjacent R779/R786/R873 boundaries were checked through indexed retrieval metadata without opening their knowledge bodies.

assignments.title: When hardware-supported 2:4 structured sparsity accelerates matrix inference end to end
assignments.finite_question: For NVIDIA Ampere-era sparse Tensor Core inference, when does a 2:4 weight pattern deliver a useful measured end-to-end gain over dense Tensor Core execution after accounting for supported dimensions/types, pruning and fine-tuning quality, sparse metadata/representation, batch size, and runtime tactic choice? Which conclusions follow from hardware peak rates, which follow from published model measurements, and which cannot transfer to GPUs without the documented sparse instruction path?
assignments.breadth_and_counterevidence: Compare the sparse MMA mechanism and its 2:4 eligibility constraints with dense execution, then relate those to the published A100/TensorRT network measurements at their stated batch sizes and timing boundaries. Cover at least one sparse win and the dense-selected/slower regime documented by the runtime or source. Record matrix role and dimensions, datatype/accumulation, batch, compression or preprocessing boundary, model accuracy metric, and architecture/runtime version where the sources provide them; mark missing fields explicitly. Distinguish theoretical 2x math throughput from layer speed and whole-network speed, and accuracy after pruning/fine-tuning from unchanged dense-model accuracy. Close with a short evaluation checklist for a different accelerator that has explicit sparse-matrix hardware support, clearly labeled as a hypothesis framework rather than an Intel/Arc prediction.
assignments.novelty_guard: This is the fixed hardware-defined 2:4 pattern and sparse Tensor Core tactic crossover, not general sparse matrix format selection, sparse storage, dense GEMM tiling, ASIC dataflow, or new precision. R778 covers SpMV/SpMM format conversion and reuse; R563/R564/R701 cover Strata dense or grouped-GEMM boundaries; R873 covers dense fully-connected ASIC dataflow. Keep those as metadata-only exclusions and do not reopen their bodies. No implementation, pruning, model change, local GPU run, adoption recommendation, XeStrata use, or inferred Arc capability is in scope.
assignments.report_budget: 1,400-1,700 substantive words, no more than 6 primary URLs, one table linking hardware eligibility to layer/network evidence, and explicit favorable and unfavorable cases with device, batch, accuracy, and timing boundaries.
prerequisites: Public access to the Ampere architecture whitepaper, original Sparse Tensor Core study, and official TensorRT/benchmark documentation listed below.
No local GPU, model, code, build, test, profiler, or process result is required.
assignments.prerequisite_evidence: The NVIDIA A100 whitepaper, the original arXiv Sparse Tensor Core paper, the NVIDIA inference benchmark blog, and current TensorRT sparsity documentation are publicly accessible primary sources.
